exact_recap:
THIS WEEK IN AUSTIN

Bus routes return in stages
Three of the four bus routes placed on detour at the start of the week are back on their normal paths by Friday’s cutoff. A maintenance closure began the disruption; partial corridor reopening restored two routes, and a third subsequently returned. That leaves one route on detour with no return date set. The week brought substantial restoration of normal routing, but the disruption has not fully ended.
Sources: Synthetic bus disruption notice; Synthetic bus access bulletin; Synthetic bus operations update.

A patient transfer plan takes shape
The clinic’s planned closure after its lease ends this month now comes with a signed agreement to transfer existing patients to two partners. The agreement gives the closure a defined transfer plan, while leaving appointment timing unsettled: current appointment dates are not guaranteed. A transfer agreement is in place; that does not establish that patients have already transferred or that their schedules will be preserved.
Sources: Synthetic clinic notice; Synthetic clinic transition agreement.

Water notice ends within a limited scope
The facility-specific boil-water notice issued after filter damage ended this week following repairs and compliant samples. The change is concrete: the notice that applied during repairs and testing has been lifted. Its scope matters as much as its resolution. The clearance applies to this facility; other infrastructure was not evaluated, so the result provides no basis for a broader claim about infrastructure conditions.
Sources: Synthetic waterworks inspection; Synthetic waterworks clearance.
